verdicts.why: "(plural)" glosses the 들 marker, which the seed target "my friends" renders only as the plural -s.
"not know" is a literal gloss of 모르; the seed renders it as "I'm not sure".
"do" glosses 할, but the seed target has "I'm going to practise" with no standalone "do".
"more" glosses 더, but the seed renders 더 잘 as "better".
"well" glosses 잘, but the seed renders 더 잘 as "better".
"the reason" glosses 이유, but the seed target says "That is why".
The words are all in "you think that it's so good", but "that" and "so" sit between them.
"when you want" is a literal gloss, but the seed target says "as soon as you want".
"how" glosses 어떻게, but the seed target has "What would you do".
"wanted to (past)" carries a tense annotation; the seed has "wanted to".
"all" glosses 모든, but the seed has "everything".
"mind" is a literal gloss of 신경 쓰지; the seed says "don't care".
"the act of" glosses 는 것, which the seed renders as "waking up".
"I (past)" glosses 어요 as pro-drop and tense; the seed has "I started".
"my words" glosses 제 말, but the seed target says "what I mean".
"the matter of" glosses 데, which the seed absorbs into "deal with the arrangements".
"only" and "the job" are in the seed but separated by "had to do the most important".
"the (object)" glosses the 를 particle; the seed has "the story".
"in / to" glosses the 에 particle; the seed has "in her bag", so "in / to" is not a substring.
"isn't enough" is a literal gloss, but the seed says "don't have enough time".
